collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — RELATIONSHIPS, SINGLEHOOD AND FAMILY (FAM2-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Couples of every kind, courting, quarrels, separations without blame, widowhood and second loves, happily single and childfree villagers, single parents, grandparents, siblings, chosen and extended families, and affection that isn't romantic. Nobody has to love, marry or have children, everyone may say no to affection, and a player's choice never obliges a villager to anything.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks two adult siblings (where the game records it); any sexes)

collection.description: A grown sibling challenges a villager to race to the rock like when they were little: race, or just sit and remember.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) and (friend) are grown now, but (subject), the older one, still remembers teaching (friend) to swim, to climb, to tie a knot. Today, walking past the lagoon, (friend) suddenly says, "Race you to the rock. Like when we were little."

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: They race, splashing and spluttering and laughing like children. (friend) wins, easily. (subject) stands in the water, puffing. "I used to win every time," (subject.he/she) says. "I know," says (friend). "You taught me." They float on their backs for a long time, looking at the sky, not saying much. The sky looks the same as it did when they were children.

"I know," says (friend). "You taught me." They float on their backs for a long time, looking at the sky, not saying much. The sky looks the same as it did when they were children.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: "I'm too old to race," says (subject), sitting down on the bank. (friend) sits beside (subject.him/her). They talk about when they were little: the crab that bit (friend)'s toe, the time (subject) fell out of the mango tree, the storm they hid from under a canoe. They laugh so much the whole beach can hear. Then they walk home together, slower than they used to.
